subproblem.title: Mollification of an integrable function by a continuous compactly supported kernel is continuous
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be any set (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure), let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable on S (with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to S), and let φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be continuous with compact support. Then the function x ↦ ∫_S u(y)φ(x − y) dy is continuous on ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid n)) (φ u : Euclid n → ℝ), IntegrableOn u S → Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → Continuous (fun x => ∫ y in S, u y * φ (x - y))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph of the parent proof ("w is continuous (dominated convergence, φ continuous and bounded)"), for a general set S. This is what makes u − w integrable on B_{R+s}(0) in the parent assembly.
1. (Bound for φ.) φ is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: fix K with |φ(x)| ≤ K for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
2. (Measurability.) Let μ_S be Lebesgue measure restricted to S and F(x, y) := u(y)φ(x − y). For each x, y ↦ F(x, y) is μ_S-a.e.-strongly measurable: u is (it is μ_S-integrable) and y ↦ φ(x − y) is continuous.
3. (Domination.) For all x and y, |F(x, y)| = |u(y)|·|φ(x − y)| ≤ K·|u(y)|.
4. (Integrable dominant.) y ↦ K·|u(y)| is μ_S-integrable, since |u| is.
5. (Continuity in the parameter.) For every y, x ↦ u(y)φ(x − y) is continuous, φ being continuous.
6. (Conclusion.) By continuity of parametric integrals under an integrable domination (continuous_of_dominated, with bound(y) = |u(y)|·K), x ↦ ∫ F(x, y) dμ_S(y) = ∫_S u(y)φ(x − y) dy is continuous. ∎

subproblem.title: Fubini identity: pairing u − u∗φ with a test function equals the φ-average of translation differences
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be a measurable set (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure), and let φ, u, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ. Assume φ is continuous with compact support and ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ = 1, u is integrable on S, g is continuous with compact support, and g(x) = 0 for every x ∉ S. Then ∫_{ℝⁿ} (u(x) − ∫_S u(y)φ(x − y) dy)·g(x) dx = ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(z)·(∫_S u(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dy) dz.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid n)) (φ u g : Euclid n → ℝ), MeasurableSet S → Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ y, φ y = 1 → IntegrableOn u S → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, x ∉ S → g x = 0) → ∫ x, (u x - ∫ y in S, u y * φ (x - y)) * g x = ∫ z, φ z * ∫ y in S, u y * (g y - g (y + z))

Source: steps 1(a) and 1(c) of the parent proof (Fubini and translation invariance turn ∫ w g into ∫ ū(y)∫ φ(z)g(y + z) dz dy; then ∫φ = 1 and a second Fubini), stated for a general measurable set S and continuous compactly supported φ, g.
Notation: ū := 1_S·u (Set.indicator S u); w(x) := ∫_S u(y)φ(x − y) dy; unlabeled integrals are over ℝⁿ with Lebesgue measure.
1. (Preliminaries.) ū is integrable on ℝⁿ (integrable_indicator_iff; S measurable, u integrable on S). φ and g are continuous with compact support, hence integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport) and bounded: fix K_φ, K_g with |φ| ≤ K_φ and |g| ≤ K_g everywhere (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
2. (Replacing S-integrals by integrals of ū.) Since 1_S(y)·u(y)·c(y) = ū(y)·c(y) for every function c and S is measurable (integral_indicator): w(x) = ∫ ū(y)φ(x − y) dy for every x, and ∫_S u(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dy = ∫ ū(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dy for every z. Moreover (u(x) − w(x))·g(x) = ū(x)g(x) − w(x)g(x) for every x: if x ∈ S then u(x) = ū(x); if x ∉ S then g(x) = 0 by hypothesis and both sides vanish.
3. (First Fubini.) Let F(x, y) := ū(y)·φ(x − y)·g(x) on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ. F is a.e.-strongly measurable for the product measure ((x, y) ↦ ū(y) by AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd; (x, y) ↦ φ(x − y) and (x, y) ↦ g(x) are continuous), and |F(x, y)| ≤ K_φ·|g(x)|·|ū(y)|, which is integrable on the product (Integrable.mul_prod applied to |g| and |ū|). Hence F is integrable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ (Integrable.mono'). Consequently:
   (a) w(x)g(x) = ∫ F(x, y) dy for every x (integral_mul_const), and x ↦ w(x)g(x) is integrable (Integrable.integral_prod_left);
   (b) for every y, ∫ φ(x − y)g(x) dx = ∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz, by translation invariance of Lebesgue measure applied to z ↦ φ(z)g(z + y) (integral_sub_right_eq_self, noting g(x − y + y) = g(x)); hence ∫ F(x, y) dx = ū(y)·∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz (integral_const_mul), and y ↦ ū(y)·∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz is integrable (Integrable.integral_prod_right together with this identity);
   (c) by Fubini (integral_integral_swap), ∫ w(x)g(x) dx = ∫∫ F(x, y) dy dx = ∫∫ F(x, y) dx dy = ∫ ū(y)(∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz) dy.
4. (Inner identity.) For every y, z ↦ φ(z)g(y) and z ↦ φ(z)g(z + y) are integrable (φ integrable; g bounded and continuous), so ∫ φ(z)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dz = g(y)·∫φ − ∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz = g(y) − ∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz, using ∫φ = 1 and y + z = z + y.
5. (Second Fubini.) Let H(z, y) := φ(z)·(ū(y)·(g(y) − g(y + z))). H is a.e.-strongly measurable on the product (as in step 3), and |H(z, y)| ≤ 2K_g·|φ(z)|·|ū(y)| since |g(y) − g(y + z)| ≤ 2K_g; the right side is integrable on the product (Integrable.mul_prod), so H is integrable. By step 2, Fubini (integral_integral_swap), integral_const_mul and step 4:
   ∫ φ(z)(∫_S u(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dy) dz = ∫∫ H(z, y) dy dz = ∫∫ H(z, y) dz dy = ∫ ū(y)(∫ φ(z)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dz) dy = ∫ ū(y)(g(y) − ∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz) dy.
6. (Assembly.) x ↦ ū(x)g(x) is integrable (ū integrable, g measurable and bounded: Integrable.mul_bdd). By step 2, 3(a) and 3(c), the left side equals ∫ ūg − ∫ wg = ∫ ūg − ∫ ū(y)(∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz) dy. By step 5 and the integrability in 3(b) (integral_sub), the right side equals ∫ ū(y)g(y) dy − ∫ ū(y)(∫ φ(z)g(z + y) dz) dy. The two expressions coincide. ∎

subproblem.title: Smooth, uniformly bounded, a.e.-convergent approximation of a bounded measurable function supported in a ball
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and R, δ ∈ ℝ with δ > 0 (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure), and let g₀ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be measurable with |g₀(x)| ≤ 1 for all x and g₀(x) = 0 whenever ‖x‖ ≥ R. Then there is a sequence (G_j)_{j∈ℕ} of functions ℝⁿ → ℝ such that every G_j is smooth (C^∞) with compact support, tsupport G_j ⊆ B_{R+δ}(0), |G_j(x)| ≤ 1 for all j and x, and G_j(x) → g₀(x) as j → ∞ for Lebesgue-almost every x ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R δ : ℝ) (g₀ : Euclid n → ℝ), 0 < δ → Measurable g₀ → (∀ x, |g₀ x| ≤ 1) → (∀ x, R ≤ ‖x‖ → g₀ x = 0) → ∃ G : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ, (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (G j)) ∧ (∀ j, HasCompactSupport (G j)) ∧ (∀ j, tsupport (G j) ⊆ ball 0 (R + δ)) ∧ (∀ j x, |G j x| ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Euclid n)), Tendsto (fun j => G j x) atTop (𝓝 (g₀ x))

No assumption on n is needed (n = 0 included).
0. (Integrability of g₀.) If x ∉ B_R(0) then ‖x‖ ≥ R, so g₀(x) = 0. On B_R(0), a set of finite measure, g₀ is measurable and bounded by 1, hence integrable (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded); its support lies in B_R(0), so g₀ is integrable on ℝⁿ (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset), in particular locally integrable.
1. (A normalized bump.) Let b be the ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = 1/4 and rOut = 1/2 (ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional, so Mathlib provides HasContDiffBump). Then b is C^∞, 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, support b = B_{1/2}(0), and b has compact support, hence is integrable. I := ∫ b > 0 by integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, because support b is a nonempty open ball, which has positive measure (measure_ball_pos). Put ρ := b/I. Then ρ is C^∞, 0 ≤ ρ ≤ 1/I, ρ(x) = 0 whenever ‖x‖ ≥ 1/2, and ∫ρ = I/I = 1.
2. (Rescaled mollifiers.) For ε > 0 put ψ_ε(x) := (εⁿ)⁻¹·ρ(ε⁻¹x). Then ψ_ε is C^∞ (a constant times ρ composed with the linear map x ↦ ε⁻¹x); ψ_ε ≥ 0; ψ_ε(x) = 0 whenever ‖x‖ ≥ ε/2 (then ‖ε⁻¹x‖ = ε⁻¹‖x‖ ≥ 1/2); |ψ_ε(x)| ≤ (1/I)/εⁿ; ψ_ε has compact support (it vanishes outside closedBall(0, ε)); and ∫ψ_ε = (εⁿ)⁻¹·εⁿ·∫ρ = 1 by the scaling law ∫ f(ε⁻¹x) dx = ε^{dim ℝⁿ}·∫f (Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul_of_nonneg) with dim ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). In particular ψ_ε is integrable and ∫ ψ_ε(x − y) dy = ∫ψ_ε = 1 for every x (integral_sub_left_eq_self).
3. (The sequence.) θ_j := δ/(j + 2) satisfies 0 < θ_j < δ (as j + 2 ≥ 2 > 1) and θ_j → 0. Define G_j := g₀ ⋆ ψ_{θ_j}, the convolution with respect to the bilinear map ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ and Lebesgue measure, so that G_j(x) = ∫ g₀(y)·ψ_{θ_j}(x − y) dy (convolution_def).
4. (Smoothness.) ψ_{θ_j} is C^∞ with compact support and g₀ is locally integrable, so G_j is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right).
5. (Support.) Let ‖x‖ ≥ R + θ_j/2. For each y, either ‖y‖ ≥ R, so g₀(y) = 0, or ‖y‖ < R, so ‖x − y‖ ≥ ‖x‖ − ‖y‖ > θ_j/2 and ψ_{θ_j}(x − y) = 0. Thus the integrand vanishes identically and G_j(x) = 0. Hence support G_j ⊆ closedBall(0, R + θ_j/2), which is compact, so G_j has compact support; and since this closed ball is closed, tsupport G_j ⊆ closedBall(0, R + θ_j/2) ⊆ B_{R+δ}(0) because θ_j/2 < δ.
6. (Uniform bound.) |G_j(x)| ≤ ∫ |g₀(y)·ψ_{θ_j}(x − y)| dy ≤ ∫ ψ_{θ_j}(x − y) dy = 1, using |g₀| ≤ 1, ψ_{θ_j} ≥ 0, integrability of y ↦ ψ_{θ_j}(x − y) (Integrable.comp_sub_left) and step 2.
7. (Convergence at Lebesgue points.) Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is uniformly locally doubling (Mathlib instance for additive Haar measures on finite-dimensional spaces). By the Lebesgue differentiation theorem in the form IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub (for the locally integrable g₀, with K = 1), for a.e. x: for every sequence of radii r_j → 0 through positive values and centres c_j with x ∈ closedBall(c_j, r_j), the averages ⨍_{closedBall(c_j, r_j)} |g₀(y) − g₀(x)| dy tend to 0. Fix such an x and use c_j := x, r_j := θ_j. Apply the approximate-identity lemma tendsto_integral_smul_of_tendsto_average_norm_sub with sets a_j := closedBall(x, θ_j), kernels k_j(y) := ψ_{θ_j}(x − y) and constant K₀ := (1/I)·|closedBall(0, 1)|, checking its hypotheses for every j:
   (a) ⨍_{a_j} |g₀ − g₀(x)| → 0 (just shown);
   (b) g₀ is integrable on a_j;
   (c) ∫ k_j = 1 (step 2), so ∫ k_j → 1;
   (d) support k_j ⊆ a_j, because k_j(y) ≠ 0 forces ‖x − y‖ < θ_j/2 ≤ θ_j;
   (e) |k_j(y)| ≤ (1/I)/θ_jⁿ = K₀/|closedBall(x, θ_j)|, because |closedBall(x, r)| = rⁿ·|closedBall(0, 1)| for r ≥ 0 (Measure.addHaar_real_closedBall' with dim ℝⁿ = n) and 0 < |closedBall(0, 1)| < ∞.
   The lemma gives ∫ k_j(y)·g₀(y) dy → g₀(x), i.e. G_j(x) → g₀(x). As this holds for a.e. x, the sequence (G_j) has all the required properties. ∎

subproblem.title: Translation bound for smooth tests from the variation hypothesis (FTC along segments and Fubini)
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ρ, V, M ∈ ℝ, u, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ and v ∈ ℝⁿ, where ℝⁿ = Euclid n carries Lebesgue measure. Assume u is integrable on the open ball B_ρ(0), and |∫_{B_ρ(0)} u(y)·Df(y)(z) dy| ≤ V‖z‖K for every smooth (C^∞) compactly supported f : ℝⁿ → ℝ with tsupport f ⊆ B_ρ(0), every z ∈ ℝⁿ and every K ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| ≤ K for all y. Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be smooth with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ B_{ρ−‖v‖}(0) and |g(y)| ≤ M for all y. Then |∫_{B_ρ(0)} u(y)(g(y + v) − g(y)) dy| ≤ V‖v‖M.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(b)–(d) of the parent proof (fundamental theorem of calculus along the segments τ ↦ y + τz, Fubini on ℝⁿ × [0, 1], and the variation hypothesis applied to the translates f_{τ,z} = g(· + τz)), isolated for one translation vector v, a general radius ρ and a general bound M.
Notation: B := B_ρ(0) (open ball); Dg := fderiv ℝ g; λ_B := Lebesgue measure restricted to B; λ_1 := Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, 1] = Set.uIoc 0 1 (a finite measure).
1. (Bounds for Dg.) g is C^∞, so g is differentiable and Dg : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, since ∞ ≠ 0); as g has compact support, so does Dg (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). A continuous compactly supported function is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): fix K_D with ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ K_D for all x. Hence |Dg(x)(v)| ≤ ‖Dg(x)‖·‖v‖ ≤ K_D‖v‖ for all x.
2. (FTC along segments.) Fix y ∈ ℝⁿ. The curve τ ↦ y + τv has derivative v at every τ ∈ ℝ, so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) τ ↦ g(y + τv) has derivative Dg(y + τv)(v) at every τ. The map τ ↦ Dg(y + τv)(v) is continuous (Dg continuous, evaluation at the fixed vector v), hence interval integrable on [0, 1]. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt), g(y + v) − g(y) = g(y + 1·v) − g(y + 0·v) = ∫_0^1 Dg(y + τv)(v) dτ.
3. (Integrability on (0, 1] × B.) Let Φ(τ, y) := u(y)·Dg(y + τv)(v). Φ is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ_1 ⊗ λ_B: y ↦ u(y) is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ_B (u is integrable on B), hence (τ, y) ↦ u(y) is a.e.-strongly measurable for the product (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd), and (τ, y) ↦ Dg(y + τv)(v) is continuous. By step 1, |Φ(τ, y)| ≤ K_D‖v‖·|u(y)|, and (τ, y) ↦ K_D‖v‖·|u(y)| is integrable for λ_1 ⊗ λ_B because |u| is λ_B-integrable and λ_1 is finite (Integrable.comp_snd). Hence Φ is λ_1 ⊗ λ_B-integrable (Integrable.mono').
4. (Fubini.) By step 2, u(y)(g(y + v) − g(y)) = ∫_0^1 Φ(τ, y) dτ for every y (the constant u(y) moves inside the interval integral, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul). By step 3 and Fubini for an interval integral against a σ-finite measure (intervalIntegral_integral_swap),
   ∫_B u(y)(g(y + v) − g(y)) dy = ∫_B ∫_0^1 Φ(τ, y) dτ dy = ∫_0^1 X(τ) dτ,  where X(τ) := ∫_B u(y)·Dg(y + τv)(v) dy.
5. (Variation bound for each translate.) Fix τ ∈ (0, 1] and put f_τ(y) := g(y + τv). Then:
   (a) f_τ is C^∞ (g composed with the smooth map y ↦ y + τv);
   (b) f_τ = g ∘ T_τ for the homeomorphism T_τ(y) := y + τv (Homeomorph.addRight (τ • v)), so f_τ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph) and tsupport f_τ = T_τ⁻¹(tsupport g) (tsupport_comp_eq_preimage);
   (c) tsupport f_τ ⊆ B: if y ∈ tsupport f_τ then y + τv ∈ tsupport g ⊆ B_{ρ−‖v‖}(0), so ‖y + τv‖ < ρ − ‖v‖; since 0 < τ ≤ 1, ‖τv‖ = τ‖v‖ ≤ ‖v‖; hence ‖y‖ ≤ ‖y + τv‖ + ‖τv‖ < (ρ − ‖v‖) + ‖v‖ = ρ;
   (d) |f_τ(y)| = |g(y + τv)| ≤ M for all y;
   (e) Df_τ(y) = Dg(y + τv) for all y (derivative of a translate, fderiv_comp_add_right).
   The hypothesis applied with f := f_τ, z := v and K := M gives |∫_B u(y)·Df_τ(y)(v) dy| ≤ V‖v‖M, i.e. by (e), |X(τ)| ≤ V‖v‖M.
6. (Conclusion.) By step 5, ‖X(τ)‖ ≤ V‖v‖M for every τ ∈ Ι(0, 1) = (0, 1], so the interval-integral estimate intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const gives |∫_0^1 X(τ) dτ| ≤ V‖v‖M·|1 − 0| = V‖v‖M. Together with step 4, |∫_B u(y)(g(y + v) − g(y)) dy| ≤ V‖v‖M. No sign condition on ρ, V or M is needed (if ρ − ‖v‖ ≤ 0 then g = 0 and every f_τ = 0 is still admissible). ∎

5. (Dominated convergence on B.) The functions hG_j are μ_B-a.e.-strongly measurable (h is, and G_j is continuous); |hG_j| ≤ |h|, which is μ_B-integrable; and hG_j → hg₀ μ_B-a.e., because Lebesgue-a.e. convergence implies μ_B-a.e. convergence (ae_restrict_of_ae). subproblem.title: Claim A: the pairing of u − u∗φ with a smooth test function bounded by 1 is at most sV
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, R, s, V ∈ ℝ with R > 0, s > 0, 2s < R and V ≥ 0, let φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be smooth with φ ≥ 0, tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0) and ∫φ = 1, and let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ be integrable on B_{2R}(0) (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure). Assume |∫_{B_{2R}(0)} u(y)·Df(y)(z) dy| ≤ V‖z‖M for every smooth compactly supported f : ℝⁿ → ℝ with tsupport f ⊆ B_{2R}(0), every z ∈ ℝⁿ and every M ∈ ℝ with |f| ≤ M everywhere. Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be smooth with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ B_{R+s}(0) and |g(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then |∫_{ℝⁿ} (u(x) − w(x))·g(x) dx| ≤ sV, where w(x) := ∫_{B_{2R}(0)} u(y)φ(x − y) dy.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (Claim A, parts (a)–(e)) of the parent proof; the Fubini/translation computation of 1(a), 1(c) is the sibling pairing_identity and the FTC-plus-variation estimate of 1(b)–(d) is the sibling translate_test.
1. (φ has compact support; g vanishes off B_{2R}(0).) tsupport φ is closed and contained in B_s(0) ⊆ closedBall(0, s), which is compact, so tsupport φ is compact: φ has compact support. φ is continuous (it is C^∞) and therefore integrable. Since s > 0 and 2s < R we have s < R, so R + s ≤ 2R and tsupport g ⊆ B_{R+s}(0) ⊆ B_{2R}(0); thus g(x) = 0 for every x ∉ B_{2R}(0) (such x is not in tsupport g). (R > 0 also follows from s > 0 and 2s < R and is not used separately; smoothness of φ is used only through continuity.)
2. (Fubini identity.) Apply pairing_identity with S := B_{2R}(0) (an open, hence measurable, set), φ (continuous, compactly supported, ∫φ = 1), u (integrable on S) and g (continuous, compactly supported, zero off S):
   ∫ (u(x) − w(x))·g(x) dx = ∫ φ(z)·I(z) dz,  where I(z) := ∫_{B_{2R}(0)} u(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dy.
3. (Pointwise bound: |φ(z)I(z)| ≤ φ(z)·sV for every z.) If φ(z) = 0 both sides are 0. Otherwise z ∈ support φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(0), so ‖z‖ < s. From 2s < R we get ‖z‖ < s < R − s, hence R + s < 2R − ‖z‖ and tsupport g ⊆ B_{R+s}(0) ⊆ B_{2R−‖z‖}(0). Apply translate_test with ρ := 2R, V, M := 1, u, g and v := z; its hypotheses hold: u is integrable on B_{2R}(0); the variation hypothesis of the present theorem is literally the one required there with ρ = 2R; g is smooth with compact support; tsupport g ⊆ B_{2R−‖z‖}(0); |g| ≤ 1. It gives |∫_{B_{2R}(0)} u(y)(g(y + z) − g(y)) dy| ≤ V‖z‖·1. Since u(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) = −u(y)(g(y + z) − g(y)), I(z) is the negative of that integral, so |I(z)| ≤ V‖z‖ ≤ Vs = sV (V ≥ 0 and ‖z‖ ≤ s). As φ(z) ≥ 0, |φ(z)I(z)| = φ(z)|I(z)| ≤ φ(z)·sV.
4. (Integration.) z ↦ φ(z)·sV is integrable (φ integrable), so by step 3 and the norm bound for integrals (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le), |∫ φ(z)I(z) dz| ≤ ∫ φ(z)·sV dz = (∫φ)·sV = sV. By step 2 this is |∫ (u(x) − w(x))g(x) dx| ≤ sV. ∎
